findings.claim: The official MemCompiler project page now gives an exact Hugging Face model identifier and explicitly describes task memory M as retrieved once at episode start, with per-step EXPERIENCE/BRIEF/HYBRID/NOACTION compilation. This strengthens the public artifact chain beyond a generic 'model exists' claim.
findings.scope_guard: The project page identifies a model artifact but does not bind it to an immutable model revision/digest, Table 3 run manifest, or the ScienceWorld memory-database bytes.

findings.claim: The exact public main tree contains code and the ScienceWorld test split but no committed memory-bank/database snapshot or run manifest; the README instead exposes MEMCOMPILER_PATH as an external path to the memory database. Therefore the evaluated candidate pool M cannot currently be reconstructed from the GitHub tree alone.
findings.scope_guard: Absence is restricted to the exact public GitHub tree inspected. It does not assert that no private, Hugging Face, or later artifact exists.

protocol_implication.name: EVALUATED_MEMORY_STATE_BUNDLE
protocol_implication.rule: A replay-ready science-agent memory result must bind source revision, model artifact revision/digest, dataset blob, memory-database digest, retrieval configuration digest and resulting candidate-pool digest. A checkpoint model alone is insufficient to identify the evaluated memory state.

direct_chat_work.performed: Created a bounded sidecar schema/semantic validator/test suite that records stable candidate IDs/digests and per-step selector provenance without injecting raw memory text into the receiver context.
